title_th: การขึ้นรถไฟฟ้า
register: Casual-polite service encounter — short, direct questions to busy transit staff; no heavy formality, but 'excuse me' and 'please' are expected

targets.why_it_matters_here: Thai finals are unreleased, so 'card' becomes 'car' and 'exit two' loses its /t/. At a ticket window the staff member hears 'car' and points you to the taxi rank; at the gate, 'my card won't work' sounds like 'my car won't work'. Miss the /t/ on 'exit' and 'next' and you get off at the wrong station with no one to ask.

Fares, top-up amounts, exit numbers, platform numbers and station counts are all numbers, and the -teen/-ty contrast lives in the final consonant plus stress. Ask to top up 'fifteen' when you mean 'fifty' and you can't get through the gate; hear 'exit forty' instead of 'exit fourteen' and you walk fifteen minutes the wrong way.

model_dialogues.label: Topping up at the ticket window and finding the right line

lines.speaker: Staff
lines.text: Hi there, how can I help?
lines.th: สวัสดีค่ะ ให้ช่วยอะไรดีคะ

lines.speaker: Learner
lines.text: I'd like to top up my card, please.
lines.th: ขอเติมเงินในบัตรหน่อยครับ

lines.speaker: Staff
lines.text: Sure. How much?
lines.th: ได้ค่ะ เติมเท่าไหร่คะ

lines.speaker: Learner
lines.text: Three hundred baht.
lines.th: สามร้อยบาทครับ

lines.speaker: Staff
lines.text: Three hundred. Here's your card back.
lines.th: สามร้อยนะคะ นี่บัตรคืนค่ะ

lines.speaker: Learner
lines.text: Thanks. Which line goes to Siam?
lines.th: ขอบคุณครับ แล้วไปสยามต้องขึ้นสายไหน

lines.speaker: Staff
lines.text: The green line. It's four stops from here.
lines.th: สายสีเขียวค่ะ จากนี่อีกสี่สถานี

lines.speaker: Learner
lines.text: Four stops. Which platform?
lines.th: สี่สถานี แล้วชานชาลาไหนครับ

lines.speaker: Staff
lines.text: Platform two — up the escalator, on the left.
lines.th: ชานชาลาสองค่ะ ขึ้นบันไดเลื่อนไป อยู่ทางซ้าย

lines.speaker: Learner
lines.text: Platform two. Thank you!
lines.th: ชานชาลาสอง ขอบคุณครับ

model_dialogues.label: The gate won't open — low balance, a closed interchange, and the wrong exit

lines.speaker: Learner
lines.text: Excuse me, the gate won't open.
lines.th: ขอโทษครับ ประตูไม่เปิด

lines.speaker: Staff
lines.text: Let me tap it here. Ah — you've only got twelve baht left.
lines.th: ขอแตะดูหน่อยนะคะ อ๋อ เหลือแค่สิบสองบาทเอง

lines.speaker: Learner
lines.text: Only twelve? I topped up yesterday.
lines.th: แค่สิบสองเองเหรอ ผมเพิ่งเติมไปเมื่อวานนี้เอง

lines.speaker: Staff
lines.text: The trip from the airport took most of it. You'll need at least fifty to get to Asok.
lines.th: ขามาจากสนามบินกินไปเกือบหมดค่ะ จะไปอโศกต้องมีอย่างน้อยห้าสิบ

lines.speaker: Learner
lines.text: Okay. Can I top up here?
lines.th: โอเคครับ เติมตรงนี้ได้ไหม

lines.speaker: Staff
lines.text: Not at the gate. The machine's over there, next to the map.
lines.th: ตรงประตูไม่ได้ค่ะ ตู้อยู่ตรงโน้น ข้างๆ แผนที่

lines.speaker: Learner
lines.text: Sorry, next to the map?
lines.th: ขอโทษครับ ข้างแผนที่ใช่ไหม

lines.speaker: Staff
lines.text: That's right. It takes cash or card — twenty and fifty baht notes.
lines.th: ใช่ค่ะ ใช้ได้ทั้งเงินสดและบัตร แบงก์ยี่สิบกับห้าสิบ

lines.speaker: Learner
lines.text: Got it. Is Asok on this line?
lines.th: เข้าใจแล้วครับ แล้วอโศกอยู่สายนี้ไหม

lines.speaker: Staff
lines.text: No, this is the blue line. Normally you'd change at Sukhumvit, but the interchange is closed for maintenance today.
lines.th: ไม่ค่ะ นี่สายสีน้ำเงิน ปกติต้องไปเปลี่ยนสายที่สุขุมวิท แต่วันนี้จุดเชื่อมปิดซ่อม

lines.speaker: Learner
lines.text: Closed? So how do I get there?
lines.th: ปิดเหรอครับ แล้วผมจะไปยังไงดี

lines.speaker: Staff
lines.text: Go one more stop to Phetchaburi and walk across, or take the number thirteen bus outside exit three.
lines.th: นั่งต่ออีกสถานีไปเพชรบุรีแล้วเดินข้ามไป หรือขึ้นรถเมล์สายสิบสามหน้าทางออกสามก็ได้

lines.speaker: Learner
lines.text: Sorry, could you say that again, slowly?
lines.th: ขอโทษครับ พูดอีกทีช้าๆ ได้ไหม

lines.speaker: Staff
lines.text: One more stop to Phetchaburi, then walk. It's about five minutes.
lines.th: นั่งต่ออีกหนึ่งสถานีไปเพชรบุรี แล้วเดินเอา ประมาณห้านาทีค่ะ

lines.speaker: Learner
lines.text: Five minutes. Which exit for the walkway?
lines.th: ห้านาที แล้วทางเดินนี่ออกทางออกไหนครับ

lines.speaker: Staff
lines.text: Exit two. Just follow the signs to the skywalk.
lines.th: ทางออกสองค่ะ เดินตามป้าย skywalk ไปเลย

lines.speaker: Learner
lines.text: Exit two, not exit three?
lines.th: ทางออกสอง ไม่ใช่ทางออกสามใช่ไหมครับ

lines.speaker: Staff
lines.text: Exit two for the walkway. Exit three is the bus stop.
lines.th: ทางออกสองคือทางเดินค่ะ ส่วนทางออกสามคือป้ายรถเมล์

lines.speaker: Learner
lines.text: Thanks a lot. That really helps.
lines.th: ขอบคุณมากครับ ช่วยได้เยอะเลย

lines.speaker: Staff
lines.text: No worries. Mind the gap when you board.
lines.th: ไม่เป็นไรค่ะ ตอนขึ้นรถระวังช่องว่างด้วยนะคะ

chunk_drills.label: Asking for the right line
examples: Which line goes to the airport?
Which line goes to the hospital?
Is this the right line for Asok?
chunk_drills.spiralled_grammar: Wh- question with present simple 'goes'; recycles place names and 'Is this the right ___ for ___?' from directions

chunk_drills.label: Topping up (numbers under pressure)
chunk_drills.pattern: Top up ___ baht, please. / How much is left on my card?
examples: How much is left on my card?
chunk_drills.spiralled_grammar: Recycles 'How much…?' and the numbers set; drills the -teen/-ty contrast inside a real transaction

chunk_drills.label: Counting stops and time
chunk_drills.pattern: How many stops to ___? / How long does it take?
examples: How many stops to Mo Chit?
chunk_drills.spiralled_grammar: Recycles time expressions and 'It takes ___ minutes'; final /s/ on 'stops' and 'minutes'

chunk_drills.label: Exits and landmarks
examples: Which exit for the bus stop?
chunk_drills.spiralled_grammar: Recycles 'Where's…?' and place vocabulary; number + final /t/ in 'exit'

chunk_drills.label: Something's wrong / getting help
examples: Excuse me, the gate won't open.
The machine won't take my note.
Sorry, could you say that again?
chunk_drills.spiralled_grammar: Negative 'won't' + base verb; recycles the clarification chunk used in every unit

listening_items.audio_text: Next station: Asok. Change here for the MRT Blue Line.
listening_items.question: What can you change to at this station?
listening_items.distractor_focus: Station name vs line name; the unreleased /k/ in 'Asok' and the final /nj/ of 'change'

listening_items.audio_text: This train terminates at Mo Chit. All passengers please alight at the next station.
listening_items.question: Do you need to get off the train? Where?
listening_items.answer: Yes — everyone gets off at the next station, Mo Chit (the last stop)
listening_items.distractor_focus: 'terminates' / 'alight' as unfamiliar announcement words; 'next' final cluster /kst/

listening_items.audio_text: That's a hundred and fifty baht altogether — fifty in change.
listening_items.question: How much do you pay?
listening_items.distractor_focus: fifteen vs fifty; 'a hundred and fifty' heard as 'a hundred and fifteen'

listening_items.audio_text: Take exit four for the mall. Exit fourteen is on the other side of the road.
listening_items.question: Which exit takes you to the mall?
listening_items.distractor_focus: four vs fourteen vs forty — stress on the final syllable

listening_items.audio_text: Trains run every three minutes, so don't push. The last train leaves at twelve thirty.
listening_items.question: What time is the last train?

guided_roleplay.learner_role: A commuter at a busy metro station with a nearly empty travel card, trying to reach a station on another line
flow: Step 1 — At the machine or window: greet and ask to top up a specific amount ('Top up a hundred baht, please').
Step 2 — Confirm the amount and the balance back ('A hundred? Yes. How much is on it now?').
Step 3 — Ask which line goes to your destination and how many stops.
Step 4 — Ask which platform, and repeat the number back to check ('Platform two?').
Step 5 — Handle one problem: the gate doesn't open, or the fare is higher than you expected. Say what's wrong in one short sentence.
Step 6 — Ask which exit you need at the far end, and confirm the exit number before you walk away.
sentence_frames: Excuse me, could I top up ___ baht?
How much is left on my card?
Sorry — platform two or platform three?
Excuse me, the gate won't open.
Sorry, could you say that again, slowly?

free_roleplay.ai_persona: Sam, a station staff member at a busy interchange. Friendly and helpful but slightly rushed, speaks at natural speed with short answers, uses real transit words ('top up', 'change at', 'terminates', 'concourse'). Never switches to Thai; will slow down and repeat if asked directly.
free_roleplay.a2_behavior: Sticks to the standard sequence: takes the top-up, states the amount and the new balance, names the line, the number of stops and the platform, and gives one exit number. Repeats any number once if the learner asks.
b1_curveballs: The top-up machine is out of order — the learner must go to the window on the other side of the concourse and explain what they need again.
The card is blocked or the gate won't open; Sam asks 'When did you last top up?' and 'How much did you put on?'
The direct line is suspended, so the learner must change lines or take a shuttle bus, and confirm the bus number.
Sam offers a choice: 'Single ticket is forty-five, or you can put fifty on the card — which do you want?'
Sam gives the exit as a letter plus a number ('Exit A3') or names a landmark the learner doesn't know, forcing a clarification question.
Sam mishears the destination and starts giving directions to a similar-sounding station; the learner must correct him politely.

roleplay_rubric.criterion: Completed the core sub-steps: topped up (or bought a ticket), found the correct line, confirmed the platform, and asked about the exit
Stated and confirmed at least two numbers accurately (amount, stops, platform or exit) so the listener could act on them
Reported the problem in one clear short sentence ('The gate won't open' / 'My card won't work')
Asked at least one clarification question instead of nodding ('Sorry, could you say that again?' / 'Exit two or exit three?')
Register stayed casual-polite: opened with 'Excuse me', kept requests short, thanked the staff member
Pronunciation: final consonants audible on 'card', 'exit', 'next', 'stop', 'left'; -teen vs -ty numbers intelligible without repetition
Stretch (B1): handled an off-script curveball — a closed line, a broken machine, or a wrong destination — and reached the destination without breaking down

register_culture_note.en: Transit staff are busy and answer in short bursts. Lead with 'Excuse me', then one clear question — long polite preambles get cut off. It is completely normal to repeat a number back ('Platform two?') or to ask someone to say it again; staff prefer that to a passenger who walks off in the wrong direction. Announcements are usually played once, so listen for the pattern: 'Next station… change here for…'

do_dont.prefer: Release the /d/: 'My card, please' — or hold the card up while you say it
'Could I top up fifty baht, please?'

do_dont.avoid: Saying 'fifteen' with stress on the first syllable (heard as 'fifty')
do_dont.prefer: Stress the end — 'fifTEEN' — and confirm: 'Fifteen, one-five.'

do_dont.avoid: Smiling and nodding when you didn't catch the exit number

register_culture_note.thai_cultural_note: Many Thai speakers nod and say 'yes, yes' rather than make a busy staff member repeat themselves — the kreng-jai instinct not to be a bother. In a station this backfires: the staff member assumes you understood and turns to the next passenger, and you end up at the wrong exit with no one to ask. Asking someone to repeat a number is treated as normal, efficient behaviour, not rudeness. Also note that outside Thailand the exit system varies — some cities use letters (Exit A) or street names instead of numbers — so always read the number or letter back before you walk.

can_do_checkpoints.statement: I can top up my travel card and say the amount clearly.
I can ask which line goes to a station and how many stops it is.
I can ask which platform and which exit I need, and repeat the number back to check.
I can understand a simple 'next station / change here' announcement.
I can explain a problem at the gate (low balance, card not working) and follow the staff member's solution.
I can cope when the route changes — a closed interchange or a shuttle bus — by asking follow-up questions until I know what to do.
My final consonants ('card', 'exit', 'next', 'stop') are audible, and my -teen/-ty numbers are understood the first time.
